//: Curation for tools/hermes_mcp_bridge.py. 'include' maps a tool-server operationId to a short description written for a small local model (USE WHEN / DO NOT USE WHEN / EXAMPLE); these tools (all of 'include'; 'core' is the default subset a profile enables) are what Hermes sees by default. 'exclude' is never exposed, even with --all. 'aliases' adds MCP tools that forward to another operationId. Every operationId must exist in the tool server's /openapi.json (checked by tests/tools/test_hermes_mcp_bridge.py). Docs: docs/HERMES_AGENT_INTEGRATION.md

include.list_designs: USE WHEN: you need the exact design names or what each design is. NOT FOR: numbers (read_metrics). ARGS: none. EXAMPLE: {}
include.read_metrics: USE WHEN: a number of ONE design: cells, area, slack, DRC, power. NOT FOR: several designs (compare_designs), why (rag_answer). ARGS: design; keys = exact keys: design__instance__count__stdcell (cell count), timing__setup__ws (WORST setup slack, ns, over all corners: use this for "worst slack"), timing__hold__ws, design__die__area (um2); or pattern = substring filter such as drc. EXAMPLE: {"design":"kv_attn_n8","keys":["design__instance__count__stdcell"]}
include.compare_designs: USE WHEN: compare or rank designs on ONE metric (most cells, slowest, smallest). NOT FOR: all numbers of one design (read_metrics). ARGS: metric = exact key from read_metrics, e.g. design__instance__count__stdcell, timing__setup__ws; designs = optional list (omit for all). EXAMPLE: {"metric":"design__instance__count__stdcell","designs":["kv_attn_n4","kv_attn_n8"]}
include.search_docs: USE WHEN: keyword lookup of a rule, command or where something is documented; read the hits and name the file. NOT FOR: numbers (read_metrics), why-questions (rag_answer). ARGS: query; k optional. EXAMPLE: {"query":"slew limit MAX_TRANSITION_CONSTRAINT","k":5}
include.rag_answer: USE WHEN: a WHY or HOW question about the repo (why does X have more flip-flops, what limits slack, what fixed congestion). Returns quoted sentences with file:line; relay them and keep the citations. NOT FOR: plain numbers (read_metrics). ARGS: question. EXAMPLE: {"question":"why does kv_attn_n8_int4 have more flip-flops than kv_attn_n8"}
include.rag_search: USE WHEN: you want ranked doc passages (file, heading, lines) to read yourself, optionally for one design. NOT FOR: a direct answer (rag_answer). ARGS: query; k, design optional. EXAMPLE: {"query":"antenna diode insertion","k":4}
include.rag_index: USE WHEN: asked about the docs search index (size, embedding model, age) or told to rebuild it. NOT FOR: answers (rag_answer). ARGS: rebuild=true only when told (takes minutes). EXAMPLE: {}
include.notes_section: USE WHEN: the user names a SECTION of a design page ("the Intuitions section of kv_attn_n8"): returns its exact text. NOT FOR: a topic keyword (explain). ARGS: design, section. EXAMPLE: {"design":"kv_attn_n8","section":"Intuitions and insights"}
include.explain: USE WHEN: "explain / how does design X work / why" about ONE design; quotes its NOTES.md on a topic. NOT FOR: numbers (read_metrics), whole-repo questions (rag_answer). ARGS: design, topic. EXAMPLE: {"design":"vision_block","topic":"how it works"}
include.run_summary: USE WHEN: "summarize the last run / how did the flow go" for a design: stages, pass/fail, key numbers. NOT FOR: raw log lines (read_log), a failure cause (diagnose). ARGS: design. EXAMPLE: {"design":"kv_attn_n8"}
include.diagnose: USE WHEN: "why did stage / check X fail" for a design or job: matches logs and metrics to a cause. NOT FOR: runs that passed (run_summary), doc questions (rag_answer). ARGS: design or job_id. EXAMPLE: {"design":"prec_fp16"}
include.suggest: USE WHEN: "what should I improve / try next" for a design: rule-based suggestions with evidence. NOT FOR: applying changes (you cannot edit files) or asking Claude. ARGS: design. EXAMPLE: {"design":"vision_block"}
include.signoff_summary: USE WHEN: is a design signoff clean: DRC, LVS, antenna, timing slack and the verdict. NOT FOR: one number (read_metrics). ARGS: design. EXAMPLE: {"design":"text_sentiment"}
include.list_logs: USE WHEN: which log files exist for a design or job. NOT FOR: reading them (read_log). ARGS: design or job_id. EXAMPLE: {"design":"kv_attn_n8"}
include.read_log: USE WHEN: "show the log / any errors in the flow log" for a design: real lines with line numbers. NOT FOR: a summary (log_digest). ARGS: design; which = flow|error|warning|make|sim|gl|stage:<name>|job:<id>; tail, grep optional. EXAMPLE: {"design":"audio_pitch","which":"error","tail":40}
include.log_digest: USE WHEN: errors, warnings and key lines of a log in a short digest. NOT FOR: full lines (read_log). ARGS: design or job_id. EXAMPLE: {"design":"kv_attn_n8"}
include.klayout_view: USE WHEN: the user wants a PICTURE of a layout in the chat ("show X met1 lower-left 50 um", "render X"). Paste the `markdown` field as given. NOT FOR: opening a window (gui_command). ARGS: design; layers = list like ["met1"]; zoom = {"bbox":[x1,y1,x2,y2]} in um. EXAMPLE: {"design":"kv_attn_n8","layers":["met1"],"zoom":{"bbox":[0,0,50,50]}}
include.open_gds: USE WHEN: "open the GDS / layout of X" on screen. NOT FOR: a picture in chat (klayout_view); window commands (gui_command). ARGS: design (a partial name such as "kv_attn" or "vision lit" is fine: the server resolves it); viewer = klayout-app|klayout|magic|png. EXAMPLE: {"design":"kv_attn","viewer":"klayout-app"}
include.gui_command: USE WHEN: ANY request about the KLayout or Magic WINDOW: "open X in klayout/magic", "show only met1 and met2", "zoom to the lower-left 50 um", "close the window", DRC on the layout. ARGS: text = the user's sentence unchanged. NOT FOR: a picture in chat (klayout_view). Partial design names in the sentence are fine ("open vision lit in klayout"). EXAMPLE: {"text":"open kv_attn_n8 in klayout"}
include.gui_status: USE WHEN: is the KLayout / Magic window running, which design is open. ARGS: none. EXAMPLE: {}
include.gui_stop: USE WHEN: close a window the tool server started, when gui_command did not. ARGS: tool = klayout|magic. EXAMPLE: {"tool":"klayout"}
include.run_make: USE WHEN: the user ORDERS a run: "Run make simulate for X", "run the full flow for X" (flow-all), make test. NOT FOR: "how do I run ..." (answer with the command text). TWO STEPS: the first call starts NOTHING and returns confirm_id and `say`: show `say` and STOP; after the user writes "yes, run <id>" call confirm_run. ARGS: target, design (omit if none). EXAMPLE: {"target":"simulate","design":"vision_block"}
include.job_status: USE WHEN: state, log tail and result of a job you started (run_make, run_experiment, whatif_run). ARGS: job_id. EXAMPLE: {"job_id":"20261007_001906-06"}
include.job_list: USE WHEN: "what jobs are running / finished". ARGS: none. EXAMPLE: {}
include.list_experiments: USE WHEN: "what can I run / list the experiments" (also demos overview). ARGS: group optional. EXAMPLE: {}
include.run_experiment: USE WHEN: the user ORDERS a named experiment ("run the experiment soc-kv"). Same two-step gate as run_make (show `say`, wait for "yes, run <id>", then confirm_run). NOT FOR: showing results (experiment_result). ARGS: id, design optional. EXAMPLE: {"id":"soc-kv"}
include.experiment_result: USE WHEN: show the results table of an experiment ("show the soc-kv results", "the precision table"). NOT FOR: starting one (run_experiment), pictures (engine_pictures). ARGS: id, job_id optional. EXAMPLE: {"id":"precision"}
include.skill_plan: USE WHEN: "give me the plan for hardening X": ordered steps of a project skill. NOT FOR: the skill text (read the skill with skills_list/skill_view). ARGS: skill, design. EXAMPLE: {"skill":"harden-design","design":"vision_block"}
include.param_info: USE WHEN: what a synthesis/timing/OpenROAD setting means and its current value. ARGS: design, key. EXAMPLE: {"design":"kv_attn_n8","key":"PL_TARGET_DENSITY_PCT"}
include.propose_change: USE WHEN: is a setting change allowed (HARD RULES check) and what the patch would be; writes nothing. ARGS: design, changes {KEY: value}. EXAMPLE: {"design":"kv_attn_n8","changes":{"PL_TARGET_DENSITY_PCT":60}}
include.whatif_run: USE WHEN: the user ORDERS a what-if flow on a COPY of a design with changed settings. Same two-step gate as run_make. ARGS: design, changes, tag. EXAMPLE: {"design":"kv_attn_n8","changes":{"PL_TARGET_DENSITY_PCT":60},"tag":"d60"}
include.whatif_result: USE WHEN: compare a finished what-if run with the committed result. ARGS: tag, design. EXAMPLE: {"tag":"d60","design":"kv_attn_n8"}
include.remember: USE WHEN: the user says "remember that ..." (saved in build/agent/memory, not in the repo). ARGS: note, topic optional. EXAMPLE: {"note":"prefers tables","topic":"style"}
include.recall: USE WHEN: "what did I tell you about ..." earlier notes or run history. ARGS: query optional. EXAMPLE: {"query":"demo"}
include.proof_local: USE WHEN: "is this local / does it send data anywhere": measured listeners and connections. ARGS: none. EXAMPLE: {}
include.show_context: USE WHEN: "what context did you get for the last turn". ARGS: none. EXAMPLE: {}
include.capability_map: USE WHEN: "what can you do / which tools do you have / help". ARGS: group optional. EXAMPLE: {}
include.confirm_run: USE WHEN: the user wrote "yes, run <id>" (6 hex characters) for a pending run. Starts exactly what that id was issued for and returns job_id. NOT FOR: any id the user did not write; never invent one. ARGS: confirm_id. EXAMPLE: {"confirm_id":"50ad87"}
include.find_pins: USE WHEN: "list the pins / ports of X matching <regex>" (from the GDS labels). NOT FOR: counts or metrics (read_metrics). ARGS: design, pattern (regex). EXAMPLE: {"design":"audio_pitch","pattern":"clk"}
include.layout_summary: USE WHEN: size and structure of a layout: top cell, die bbox (um), cell and shape counts, busiest layers. NOT FOR: a picture (klayout_view), numbers like area/slack (read_metrics). ARGS: design. EXAMPLE: {"design":"kv_attn_n4"}
include.layer_stats: USE WHEN: shape count, area and bbox of ONE GDS layer ("how many met1 shapes"). ARGS: design, layer (met1, li1, poly ...). EXAMPLE: {"design":"vision_block","layer":"met1"}
include.precheck_summary: USE WHEN: result of the ChipFoundry precheck (check name -> PASS/FAIL). ARGS: none. EXAMPLE: {}
include.health: USE WHEN: "is the tool server healthy / are Ollama, Docker, KLayout reachable". NOT FOR: privacy proof (proof_local). ARGS: none. EXAMPLE: {}
include.engine_pictures: USE WHEN: OpenROAD pictures of a finished design: heat maps, congestion, IR drop, placement density. NOT FOR: layer views (klayout_view). ARGS: design, view = congestion|placement|power|irdrop|... EXAMPLE: {"design":"kv_attn_n8","view":"congestion"}
include.demo_steps: USE WHEN: "run demo kv" or "show demo <name or number>": returns the ordered steps to narrate. NOT FOR: run_make. ARGS: name (number or name from list_demos). EXAMPLE: {"name":"kv"}
include.list_demos: USE WHEN: "list the demos": numbered menu. ARGS: none. EXAMPLE: {}
include.context_brief: USE WHEN: "what do you know about this repo and my notes": curated repo facts plus the memory digest. ARGS: none. EXAMPLE: {}
include.gui_examples: USE WHEN: "what can I say to control the KLayout / Magic window": the sentences gui_command understands. ARGS: none. EXAMPLE: {}

ask_claude.description: ESCALATE TO CLAUDE (the owner's Claude Code CLI, headless, in this repo, edit tools denied: it can read, search and run make, never edit files; costs the owner's Claude plan). POLICY: use ONLY when (a) the user asks for Claude by name, or (b) a local answer (search_docs, diagnose, explain, read_metrics) was tried and is inconclusive on a complex multi-step task. DO NOT USE for lookups, counts, simple questions or anything a local tool answers. TWO STEPS (confirm gate): the first call starts NOTHING and returns confirm_id and `say`; show it to the user and STOP; call again with the same arguments plus confirm_id only after the user replies 'yes, run <confirm_id>'. Then it returns job_id: poll claude_status until state is done and give the user Claude's report and the cost. One Claude task at a time. EXAMPLE: {"instructions":"Why does kv_attn_n16 fail hold at the slow corner? Read the run reports and explain.","design":"kv_attn_n16"}

claude_status.description: USE WHEN: you started ask_claude (or any job) and need its state; when state is done it contains Claude's report and cost. Poll until done, do not guess. EXAMPLE: {"job_id":"<id from ask_claude>"}

//core: Phase 2 (tool-calling eval): the default set a profile exposes (38 tools + the ask_claude/claude_status aliases), chosen so every question group of examples/hermes_desktop/eval_tools/cases.json has its tool. The rest of 'include' stays available (hermes mcp configure, or the bridge's --all). tools/hermes_mcp_bridge.py lists all of 'include'; scripts/hermes/setup_profile.py should write 'core' (plus aliases) into tools.include. Measured: tool_search off + no file toolset + these descriptions took a Hermes chip profile from 12.5% (8 cases) to 100% on the same 8 (build/agent/tool_eval_PLAN.md).
